newsitem.title: CHINA: Guangdong Power raises electricity rates.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Power raises electricity rates.

text.p: Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd said on Monday it had won approval from local authorities to raise its electricity rates.
The electricity price from the company's 100 percent-owned Shajiao A Power Plant has been raised to 357.30 yuan per megawatt hour, the firm said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The rate of its 51 percent-owned Zhanjiang Power Plant has been lifted to 505.03 yuan per megawatt hour, it said.
The price of the firm's 51 percent-owned Meixian B Power Plant was set at 494.62 yuan per megawatt hour, it said.
The higher rates were not subject to value-added tax, it said, adding that the new prices were effective from January 1, 1997. The statement gave no further details.

Shajiao's rate was 337.15 yuan per megawatt hour in 1996 and Zhanjiang's price stood at 492.27 yuan last year, company spokesman Zhang Dewei told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Meixian started production last March, Zhang said.
The higher rates would have little impact on the company's 1997 earnings because it raised them in line with increases in prices of fuels and transport, Zhang said.

The power supplier's net profits for the first half of 1997 were little changed from 296.10 million yuan in the year-earlier period under international accounting standards because electricity output remained almost unchanged, spokesman Cheng Chuyang said last week.

The company posted net profits of 563.75 million yuan for 1996, compared with 376.97 million based on international standards. The company attributed the earnings surge to a 30 percent jump in electricity output.
Cheng said the company planned to make an offer of 100 million new B shares to raise HK$600 million later this year.
The company would use the proceeds to finance an expansion of the Zhanjiang Plant, doubling the number of generators to four, each with 300 megawatts.
The expansion needed total investment of 3.2 billion yuan, with the third generator expected to start operation by 1999 and the fourth the year after.
The firm planned to appoint China Southern Securities Co Ltd as the chief domestic underwriter and Nomura International (HK) Ltd the global coordinator, Cheng said.

The company had 825.45 million shares outstanding at end-1996, consisting of 513.65 million non-listed shares, 98.55 million domestic currency A shares and 213.25 million hard currency B shares, said the firm's 1996 annual report.
